selection_reason: Real user-facing PHP web product where the repository is not the best deploy artifact; success depends on selecting the official release/image path, initializing DB/cache correctly, and verifying the installed app rather than just cloning master.

Rails/Postgres/Redis web product with onboarding and authenticated API verification requirements; anonymous HTTP checks are weak, and historical experience shows env/DB credential drift can break bootstrap.
Asset-management Laravel app with DB, storage, APP_KEY/env, login, dashboard, and asset-route verification; representative of config-sensitive web apps likely to expose shallow verification.

Customer-support web app with Rails, Postgres, Redis, Elasticsearch and first-run readiness concerns; historically timed out, but it is still a real web product with official self-hosting paths and no inherent external license/token blocker.

Large self-hosted DevOps web platform where the source repo is not the practical deployment artifact; success depends on choosing an official package/container path, handling heavy startup/resource needs, initial root credential discovery, and verifying real authenticated project/repository behavior.

Rails/Postgres/Redis forum product with a non-trivial official Docker launcher/bootstrap path, slow first-run initialization, admin account setup, mail-related configuration, and meaningful forum/topic verification requirements.

Team collaboration web product with database-backed initialization, server/webapp split concerns, default configuration drift, first-user/team onboarding, and authenticated channel/message baseline verification needs.

Large Rails project-management web app with official container paths but slow boot/migrations, DB/storage concerns, initial admin login, and project/work-package baseline verification; historically timed out rather than being blocked by an external license.
